blindComparison: A stranger picks the Ghost of Tsushima torii approach over phone-torii-r15, and the single specific reason is colour separation between key and fill: in the reference every shadowed plane is a distinctly cool blue-violet sitting against amber key light, so the ground reads as a modelled surface with raking shadows across it. In ours every shaded surface measures warm brown — shaded haiden facade (760,515,127,47) meanRGB [47.7,35.2,27.6], B/R 0.58; shaded plaza (152,1006,152,59) [34.2,29.8,28.1], B/R 0.82; torii-shot shaded plaza (1393,1076,203,59) [42.7,38.3,35.8], B/R 0.84 — against a spec of #4a6b8f (B/R 1.93). Combined with a flagstone plaza that carries no cast shadow from any of the fifteen-plus torii posts, stone lanterns, banners and fences standing on it, the whole plaza reads as one flat unlit brown sheet with props pasted onto it. Everything else in the frame — the torii silhouette, the building forms, the flagstone slab layout — is competitive. The light is not.

findings.shot: hero, torii, wide, valley, sun (all five)
findings.problem: Every shadowed surface in the set is warm brown. There is no cool sky-bounce anywhere in any frame. Measured at native 2532x1170, mean RGB of shaded regions: phone-hero-r15 shaded haiden facade box (760,515,127,47) = [47.7,35.2,27.6], B/R 0.58, G/R 0.74; phone-hero-r15 shaded underside of the left pavilion roof box (76,608,127,47) = [12.2,9.3,10.0], B/R 0.82; phone-hero-r15 shaded plaza far-left box (152,1006,152,59) = [34.2,29.8,28.1], B/R 0.82; phone-torii-r15 shaded plaza box (1393,1076,203,59) = [42.7,38.3,35.8], B/R 0.84. In every case R > G > B, i.e. the shadow side is the SAME hue as the key side, only darker. ARCHITECTURE.md §5 specifies shadow/ambient #4a6b8f = (74,107,143), B/R 1.93, G/R 1.45, and explicitly says 'never neutral grey'. The result is that the hero and wide frames have no colour contrast at all: a horizontal scan of the hero plaza at y=0.80 (eleven 0.04x0.03 normalized boxes from x=0.10 to x=0.90) returns luma p50 33.4, 52.9, 37.4, 39.4, 41.5, 45.4, 54.4, 17.3, 75.7, 62.6, 60.1 with meanRGB warm-brown at every single sample.
findings.why: This is the top-of-list failure that poisons everything under it. Golden-hour reference imagery lives or dies on the amber/blue split — it is the entire reason Tsushima's fields read as sunlit rather than as an orange filter. With key and fill at the same colour temperature the frame collapses to a single-hue brown wash, and every subsequent judgement (material response, aerial perspective, silhouette) is being made against mud. A viewer reads it as 'sepia filter' before they consciously notice anything else.
findings.fix: Shaded surfaces must go cool while sunlit surfaces stay warm. Verifiable targets, all measured with `node tools/probe.mjs stats` on the re-captured native frames: (a) phone-hero-r15 box (760,515,127,47) mean B/R must rise from 0.58 to >= 1.30 and G/R to >= 1.10; (b) phone-hero-r15 box (152,1006,152,59) B/R from 0.82 to >= 1.25; (c) phone-torii-r15 box (1393,1076,203,59) B/R from 0.84 to >= 1.25; (d) simultaneously, sunlit flagstone in phone-sun-r15 box (1266,702,506,23) must KEEP a warm bias, B/R <= 0.75 (it is currently 153.7/225.3 = 0.68 — do not lose this). Whole-frame saturation on hero must rise from 0.314 to >= 0.36 without whole-frame luma p50 moving more than +/-8 from its current 75.5. Do not achieve this by tinting the grade — that would cool the sunlit stone too and target (d) will catch it.
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING — disprove before acting: capture metadata reports hemiIntensity 1.02 and sunColor [1,0.412,0.134]. It is possible the ambient/hemi term is being tinted by the same warm sun colour rather than by the sky colour, so that fill and key share a hue. Ablate: force the ambient/probe contribution to pure #4a6b8f at its current intensity, re-shoot hero, and measure box (760,515,127,47). If B/R does not move, the ambient term is not what is lighting that pixel and this hypothesis is dead — report the disproof.

findings.problem: On the shrine plaza there is no readable cast shadow from anything. In phone-torii-r15, crop (0,842,886,328) shows two 2.2 m stone lanterns and the great torii's vermilion post all standing on flagstone with nothing but a small dark AO smear directly under each base — no directional shadow. In phone-wide-r15, crop (836,725,760,445) contains one vermilion torii, eight stone lanterns and a pole, and not one of the ten throws a shadow. In phone-hero-r15, crop (1393,644,760,526) and crop (1570,491,962,679) show four stone lanterns and two torii posts, again with zero cast shadow. The horizontal scan across the hero plaza at y=0.80 quoted in the previous finding returns luma p50 in a 33-62 band with only two outliers, and both outliers are explainable — 17.3 is a puddle at x=0.66 and 75.7 is a lantern light pool at x=0.74. There is no elongated dark structure anywhere on the plane. Capture metadata reports sun elevation 13 degrees, so a 2.2 m lantern should be laying down a ~9.5 m shadow and the ~8 m torii a ~35 m shadow. Note that shadows DO work elsewhere: phone-valley-r15 shows a crisp, correct fence shadow raking across the stone deck at roughly (1050,720)-(1900,950), and phone-sun-r15 crop (760,819,1139,351) shows a soft occlusion wedge from the torii post. So this is specifically about the plaza in the three shrine framings, not about shadows being globally off.
findings.why: 'Every object looks pasted onto the ground' is the exact failure named in tools/CRITIC.md, and here it is literal: fifteen-plus props sit on a flat sheet with no contact evidence beyond a grey smudge. The torii approach at low sun is the single most recognisable image in this genre and its whole graphic power is the long raking shadow bars across stone. Without them the plaza is a texture, not a place, and the frame reads as an engine test.
findings.fix: Each plaza prop must lay down a readable elongated shadow. Verifiable target on the re-captured phone-hero-r15: take a 60x30 px box centred on the flagstone point ~9 m down-sun of the near stone lantern base (base is at approximately (1574,1072) native) and an identical box the same distance cross-sun at the same screen y; the down-sun box must read at least 35% lower luma p50 than the cross-sun box. Repeat on phone-torii-r15 for the near lanterns at approximately (170,1000) and (470,1010) native. The shadow must be tight at the base (penumbra under ~4 px where the stone foot meets the flagstone) and visibly soften along its length. Re-run the eleven-box horizontal scan at y=0.80 on hero (boxes x=0.10..0.90 step 0.08, size 0.04x0.03): at least three non-adjacent boxes must drop >= 30% below the scan median, and those dips must line up with prop positions rather than with the puddle at x=0.66.
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING — disprove before acting: at 13 degrees elevation a horizontal ground plane receives N.L = sin(13) = 0.225 of the key, so removing the direct term from a ground fragment may be too small a delta to register against the ambient floor — which would mean the shadow map is correct and the problem is the key/fill ratio on near-horizontal surfaces, not the CSM. Cheap ablation: set the ambient/hemi contribution to zero for one capture and re-shoot hero. If lantern-shaped dark bars appear on the plaza, the CSM is fine and this is an exposure-ratio problem; if the plaza stays uniform, the shadow map genuinely is not reaching it. Either way report which, because it decides whether anyone should touch cascade code at all.

findings.problem: The bamboo sea — the thing the setting is built around — does not read as bamboo. In phone-wide-r15 crop (0,257,886,351) the hillside grove is a field of short, blunt, disconnected vertical yellow-olive STUBS scattered on a mauve-brown slope, with flat cut-off tops, no taper, no leaf canopy, and visible gaps between culm and ground. It reads as corn stubble or cactus, not a forest. In phone-valley-r15 crop (0,70,1013,351) — the overlook framing that exists specifically to sell this — the grove is a thin picket line of flat, hard-edged, stair-stepped vertical slabs with open sky visible between them; leaf sprigs appear only on the two or three nearest culms and nowhere in the mass. There is no layering, no depth, no canopy. Colour is wrong throughout: phone-valley-r15 box (253,187,506,117) meanRGB [182.7,159.8,112.8] and phone-hero-r15 box (127,351,253,140) meanRGB [94.4,82.5,78.2] — R > G in both, i.e. the bamboo is khaki and grey-brown, never green, and the hero sample sits at saturation 0.194 (grey mush). The hero-shot band alone covers roughly x 127-380, y 351-491 native.
findings.why: In the reference titles the bamboo grove is the signature set piece and it works because it is 80% leaf and 20% culm, layered front-to-back with real occlusion, with strong green-to-gold translucency when backlit. Ours is 100% culm, one layer deep, and colourless. At thumbnail size in the contact sheet the valley shot reads as a wheat field. This is the single largest area of the establishing frame (~12% of phone-wide-r15) and it looks broken rather than merely simple.
findings.fix: Give the grove a canopy and give it green. Verifiable targets on the re-captured frames: (a) phone-valley-r15 box (253,187,506,117) must invert its channel order to G > R with G-R >= 12, and saturation must rise from 0.397 to >= 0.45; (b) phone-hero-r15 box (127,351,253,140) saturation must rise from 0.194 to >= 0.30 and G must exceed R; (c) leaf mass must be present throughout the grove, not just on the nearest culms — `detail` (mean |Laplacian|) in phone-valley-r15 box (253,187,506,117) must rise from 5.97 to >= 9.0, indicating actual foliage structure rather than flat slabs; (d) in phone-wide-r15 box (127,351,506,176) the culm tops must stop terminating in flat blunt cuts — lumaSpread must rise from 53.3 to >= 80 as leaf clusters break up the silhouette. Budget headroom exists: the capture reports 115 draw calls against a 140 budget and 736-776 k triangles against 900 k, with bamboo-cards currently at 9875 instances / 39500 triangles (4 tris each).
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING — do not build around it: at 4 triangles per bamboo instance the current cards may be single quads carrying culm-only artwork with no leaf geometry or leaf texture at all, which would explain the total absence of canopy. Check the instance triangle count and the card's alpha content before assuming a shading or wind problem.

findings.problem: Small dark horizontal dashes float in clear, empty sky above the bamboo canopy line in four of the five frames. Clearest in phone-valley-r15 crop (51,94,405,117): roughly forty dark maroon dashes, each about 8-14 px long and 3-4 px tall, all identically horizontal, strung along a curve through open sky several hundred pixels above the nearest geometry. They are unmissable against a smooth sky — that region measures luma p1 85.5 with detail 5.95, against clean sky at the same height box (760,59,253,70) measuring luma p1 209.4 with detail 0.48. So the dashes cut local luma by ~124 levels and raise local contrast 12x over the sky they sit in. Same artifact in phone-hero-r15 crop (1772,532,760,88), phone-wide-r15 crop (0,257,886,351) where hundreds of them are strewn across the hillside grove like a swarm of flies, and phone-sun-r15 at approximately (810,680)-(960,700) and (2250,620)-(2520,710) native. In every frame the dash band follows the contour of the bamboo canopy top.
findings.why: This is the kind of defect a reviewer screenshots. It reads as dirt on the lens, dead pixels, or a broken particle system — not as art. Nothing in the reference titles has floating detached debris in a clean sky. It is present in 4 of 5 review frames including the establishing shot, so there is no framing that avoids it.
findings.fix: No detached dark elements may appear in open sky. Verifiable target: on the re-captured phone-valley-r15, box (51,94,405,117) must measure luma p1 >= 190 and detail <= 1.2 (currently 85.5 and 5.95), i.e. statistically indistinguishable from the clean-sky control box (760,59,253,70) which reads p1 209.4 / detail 0.48. Also re-check phone-hero-r15 box (1772,532,760,88) and phone-wide-r15 box (0,257,886,351) visually at native resolution for the same dash pattern.
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING — disprove in minutes, do not rebuild around it: the dash bands track the bamboo canopy contour exactly and appear only where bamboo is on the horizon, which points at the bamboo/leaf card layer rather than at petals or embers. But they are dark maroon in phone-valley-r15 and near-black in phone-wide-r15, which is also consistent with unlit sakura petal or ember cards from src/fx/Weather.js. Settle it with one ablation capture: disable the petal/ember emitters and re-shoot valley. If the dashes remain, they belong to Foliage and this file owns the fix; if they vanish, hand the finding to src/fx/Weather.js and say so.

findings.problem: The shrine plateau in the establishing frame is a featureless smeared brown plane covering roughly 45% of phone-wide-r15. Crop (1393,644,1139,526) shows it at native: the surface is a directionally-streaked brown-orange splat with obvious stretching along one axis, dressed only with thousands of tiny near-black spiky specks scattered at uniform stochastic density — no clumping, no drift, no density gradient, no worn footpaths, no debris, no moss. Measured: grass-speck field box (1823,842,354x117) meanRGB [54.9,43.0,36.8] luma p1 18.6 / p50 44.8 / p99 75.1; bare ground between specks box (1570,1053,253x70) [41.0,32.3,27.1] luma 12.9/31.8/64.6; far-right plateau box (2152,702,304x117) [64.3,52.7,44.8] luma p1 31.4 / p50 54.8 / p99 76.3. R > G > B everywhere — there is no green on the plateau at all, and moss #4e6b3c from ARCHITECTURE §5 appears nowhere. This is why phone-wide-r15 is the only washed frame in the set: capture histogram gives it p01 12, p1 18, p99 196, pctBelow16 0.458%, pctAbove240 0.005%, against phone-hero-r15 at 8.279% / 0.049% and phone-torii-r15 at 9.432% / 0.298%. The wide frame has no true black and no clean highlight; roughly a third of it lives inside a 45-level brown band.
findings.why: tools/CRITIC.md priority 8 is 'does the place look inhabited and weathered, or like a level editor with props dropped in'. This is the second. Real ground at a working shrine has beaten paths where feet go, moss in the wet corners, gravel that has been raked and scuffed, litter of leaves under the trees. Ours has a uniform sprinkle of identical dark specks on smeared mud. It is also the frame most likely to be used as a store-page or press screenshot, and it is the one frame in the set with no blacks and no highlights — priority 1.
findings.fix: Break the plateau surface up and get value range back into it. Verifiable targets on the re-captured phone-wide-r15: (a) the frame histogram must reach pctBelow16 >= 3.0% and pctAbove240 >= 0.05%, and p1 must drop from 18 to <= 8, without whole-frame luma p50 moving more than +/-10 from its current 92.8; (b) whole-frame saturation must rise from 0.232 to >= 0.29; (c) box (2152,702,304x117) lumaSpread must rise from 44.9 to >= 80 as surface variation is introduced; (d) at least one sample box on the plateau must return G > R, proving moss/damp ground exists somewhere on it. Introduce it as material and splat variation — worn paths along the processional axis where the lanterns line up, damp/moss patches near the stream edge and building drip-lines, gravel-vs-packed-earth boundaries — not as a global contrast bump, which target (a)'s p50 constraint will catch.

findings.problem: The sun disc does not read as a sun. In phone-sun-r15 the disc sits at approximately (1529,530) native and measures, box (1514,515,30x29), meanRGB [254.7,253.2,235.0], saturation 0.077, luma p50 251.9. The sky 106 px to its right, box (1620,515,51x35), measures [234.1,226.0,202.0], luma p50 225.9. So the sun is only 12% brighter than the sky immediately around it and is essentially white — B/R 0.92 — with no warmth whatsoever at a moment when the key light colour is reported as [1,0.412,0.134] (B/R 0.13). Visually, crop (1063,351,1063,527) shows it as a small soft fuzzy pale blob that reads as a bokeh smudge or a lens flare ghost, not a disc. Same in phone-valley-r15: box (919,23,51x47) meanRGB [242.3,239.0,217.5], saturation 0.103, luma p50 238.1 against a sky already at 217-225. The disc also has no defined limb and no wide falloff — it stops after about 60 px.
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE §5 non-negotiable 1 is 'a real sun disc'. Both the sun shot and the valley shot are composed around the sun, and in both it is the weakest element in frame — the lantern glow at box (1266,351,76x59) reaches luma p50 216.5 with saturation 0.285, which is more saturated and nearly as bright as the sun itself. A magic-hour sun is the brightest and warmest object in the world by orders of magnitude; when it is a pale grey dot the whole atmosphere model loses its anchor and the sky reads as a painted gradient with a sticker on it.
findings.fix: The disc must be over-range and warm. Verifiable targets on the re-captured phone-sun-r15: (a) box (1514,515,30x29) luma p50 must reach >= 254 with pctAbove240 within that box at 100%, i.e. fully clipped core; (b) the disc must be warm — mean B/R in that box must fall from 0.92 to <= 0.80 at the limb, and the annulus box (1560,515,40x29) just outside the core must read saturation >= 0.20 (currently the whole area is 0.077-0.137); (c) the surround contrast must open up — luma p50 of the core box divided by luma p50 of box (1620,515,51x35) must rise from 1.12 to >= 1.30 (achieve this by lifting the disc, not by darkening the sky: box (1620,515,51x35) luma p50 must stay within +/-12 of its current 225.9); (d) the same three targets on phone-valley-r15 box (919,23,51x47), currently luma p50 238.1 / saturation 0.103.

findings.problem: There are no god rays. phone-sun-r15 is the frame composed for exactly this test — the sun sits in the gap between two massive torii posts, with a shimenawa, hanging shide streamers, a stone lantern and a bamboo horizon all in front of it — and the gap contains no crepuscular striation at all. Three horizontal sample strips straight through the glare region, all 506x23 px: box (1266,585,506x23) detail 0.57, saturation 0.184; box (1266,644,506x23) detail 0.71, saturation 0.268; box (1266,702,506x23) detail 2.30, saturation 0.322. A `detail` (mean |Laplacian|) of 0.57-0.71 means that region is a mathematically smooth gradient — there is not one shaft edge in it. Visually, crop (1063,351,1063,527) confirms it: the entire area between the posts is an unbroken cream wash. Whole-frame the sun shot is the flattest in the set at detail 3.38.
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE §5 non-negotiable 4 is 'volumetric god rays through the torii and bamboo'. It is not delivered in the one frame built to show it. Beyond the contract, shafts are what turn a backlit gate from a flat glare into depth — they are the single strongest depth cue available at magic hour and the reason the reference titles' torii shots read as volumes of air rather than as a bright background.
findings.fix: Discrete shafts must be readable through the torii gap. Verifiable target on the re-captured phone-sun-r15: `detail` must rise from 0.57 to >= 3.0 in box (1266,585,506x23) and from 0.71 to >= 3.5 in box (1266,644,506x23), with the increase coming from radially-oriented light/dark banding rather than from grain (check by confirming detail in the clean upper sky box (300,120,400x60) does not rise by more than 0.5 over its current value). Whole-frame luma p50 must not move more than +/-10 from 159.9, and pctAbove240 must not exceed 1.0% (currently 0.138%) — no white-out.
findings.hypothesis: LABELLED HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING, AND HISTORY SAYS BE CAREFUL HERE: a previous round acted on an unverified god-ray mechanism guess and made the frame worse. Do not raise a global weight. Before changing anything, render the occluder/depth input of the pass to screen and photograph it, and confirm the torii posts, shimenawa, shide and bamboo actually appear as occluders in it. Report what that buffer looks like even if you change nothing.

findings.problem: The sakura reads as a formless pink puff, not a tree. In phone-wide-r15 crop (861,421,405x187) it is a bubblegum-pink cauliflower cloud hovering above the roofs with no visible trunk, no branch armature, and a lumpy hard silhouette. It is also the loudest thing in an otherwise muted frame: box (924,468,152x70) saturation 0.350 and luma p50 144.4, against the surrounding mid-ground box (709,515,152x70) at saturation 0.186 and luma p50 106.6 — 1.9x the saturation and +38 luma of everything near it, in a frame whose overall saturation is 0.232. At close range it is no better: phone-hero-r15 crop (127,23,810x445) shows the canopy as chunky flat blossom slabs with visible straight-cut edges and long thin horizontal slivers (cards seen near edge-on), split into hot salmon lit clusters and dead mauve-grey shadowed clusters, box (354,117,253x117) meanRGB [135.8,82.6,91.3] — note B > G, the shadowed blossom has gone cold purple. phone-torii-r15 crop (734,410,354x644) shows the same mass behind the torii as a lilac low-poly rock formation.
findings.why: Falling sakura is named in ARCHITECTURE §5 as a defining feature of the setting, and in the reference titles the trees are the most carefully art-directed objects on screen — soft translucent masses with readable branch structure and colour that stays inside the warm palette. Ours is the one element a viewer's eye goes to first and the one that most obviously reads as unfinished: a magenta smoke VFX pasted over the shrine. In the wide shot it actively damages the frame by being the only saturated thing in it.
findings.fix: Give the canopy structure and pull it back into the palette. Verifiable targets: (a) phone-wide-r15 box (924,468,152x70) saturation must drop from 0.350 to 0.22-0.28 so it no longer outshouts the frame's 0.232, while luma p50 stays within +/-15 of 144.4; (b) phone-hero-r15 box (354,117,253x117) must lose the cold-purple shadow — mean G must exceed mean B (currently G 82.6 < B 91.3) so shadowed blossom stays warm; (c) the canopy silhouette must break up — phone-hero-r15 crop (127,23,810x445) must show visible branch/twig geometry inside and at the edge of the blossom mass, and must not show straight-cut card edges or thin horizontal slivers when viewed at native resolution; (d) in phone-wide-r15 a trunk must be visible connecting canopy to ground.

findings.problem: The puddles on the flagstone plaza render as near-black voids. phone-hero-r15 crop (1114,959,405x152) and crop (1013,889,912x281) show six or more amoeba-shaped patches across the plaza; the largest, box (1304,977,89x53), measures meanRGB [18.4,13.5,11.5] with luma p50 4.1, against adjacent dry flagstone box (1177,1006,76x35) at [52.9,40.1,32.6] luma p50 43.6. The puddle is 10.6x DARKER than the stone it sits in. Its edge is a hard aliased cutout with no wet-darkened transition rim, its interior is crushed flat (p50 4.1 with detail 4.59, almost all of which is the boundary), and it carries essentially no reflection — only one of the six, at approximately (1810,1030) native, shows any warm streak at all (box (1798,1035,76x35) meanRGB [112.2,72.6,52.5]).
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE §5 names 'wet stone' as a defining surface of the setting, and physically a puddle under a 13-degree sun at magic hour is the brightest thing on the ground — it mirrors the orange sky almost specularly at that grazing angle. Inverting that so the water is the darkest thing in frame is not a subtle error: at native resolution these read as holes punched in the plaza, or as soot stains, and they undermine the one surface that could have given the flagstone a specular story.
findings.fix: Puddles must read as sky-reflecting water. Verifiable targets on the re-captured phone-hero-r15: (a) box (1304,977,89x53) luma p50 must rise from 4.1 to at least 1.5x the adjacent dry-stone control box (1177,1006,76x35) — i.e. >= 65 given the control's current 43.6 — inverting the current 0.09x ratio; (b) that box must go warm, mean B/R <= 0.75, carrying the sky/sun colour; (c) lumaSpread inside the puddle must reach >= 100 (currently 85.2, and almost all of it is the hard edge) from an actual reflected gradient; (d) the boundary must soften — a 3-8 px damp rim where the wet patch meets dry stone rather than the current 1 px cutout. Also give the dry flagstone around them a raised specular response at this grazing angle: box (1177,1006,76x35) is currently detail 9.42 but entirely diffuse.

findings.problem: The establishing frame has no foreground, no framing element and no subject scale. In phone-wide-r15 the shrine complex — the reason for the shot — occupies roughly x 700-1650, y 470-680 native, under 15% of frame area, while the right 40% of the image (x 1500-2532) is empty plateau with a fence and a bridge in it. Mountains take the top half, ground takes the bottom half, and nothing occupies the near field to give depth: the nearest object is a banner at (150,890) that reads as clutter rather than as a repoussoir. There is no leading line to the shrine even though a stone processional avenue with paired lanterns exists in the level and would provide one.
findings.why: tools/CRITIC.md priority 4. The reference titles' establishing shots always plant something dark and close in the near field — a branch, a torii leg, a rock — so the eye has a foreground, mid-ground and background to walk through. Ours is two horizontal bands with a small thing in the middle, which is why it reads flat despite containing more geometry than any other frame in the set. It is also the frame that ends up on a store page.
findings.fix: Re-frame the wide shot so it has three depth planes. Verifiable targets on the re-captured phone-wide-r15: (a) a near-field element must occupy at least 8% of frame area within the outer third of the frame and read at least 30% darker than the mid-ground (mid-ground control box (709,515,152x70) currently luma p50 106.6); (b) the shrine complex must occupy >= 25% of frame area, up from under 15%; (c) the paired-lantern processional avenue must run as a diagonal from a frame edge toward the shrine rather than sitting parallel to the bottom edge; (d) the dead right third must be either filled or cropped out — no 0.12-normalized-wide sample box in the right third may return lumaSpread below 60 (box (2152,702,304x117) currently returns 44.9).

findings.problem: The mid-distance in phone-sun-r15 is washed to near-white far too close to camera. The bamboo horizon and the wooden fence at roughly 30-60 m sit at box (1266,585,506x23) luma p50 227.2 with saturation 0.184 — they have lost essentially all contrast and colour against a sky at 225.9. The near torii posts are affected too: box (1823,410,152x293) on the large right-hand post returns detail 1.43 and lumaSpread 68, and box (1195,410,63x293) on the mid post returns detail 0.98 — these are the two largest objects in the frame and they are near-featureless flat brown slabs, with none of the wood grain that the same material clearly shows in phone-torii-r15 box (1545,410,76x293) at detail 6.20 and phone-hero-r15 box (1772,351,63x293) at detail 6.88.
findings.why: Aerial perspective should ramp over kilometres, not tens of metres. When a fence 40 m away has the same value as the sky, the scene loses its middle distance entirely and the frame becomes two planes — a brown foreground and a white void. Comparing the same torii material at detail 1.4 here versus 6.2-6.9 in the other shots shows how much surface information the haze is eating in the near field.
findings.fix: Push the haze ramp back. Verifiable targets on the re-captured phone-sun-r15: (a) box (1266,585,506x23) saturation must rise from 0.184 to >= 0.28 and luma p50 must fall from 227.2 to <= 205, restoring separation from the sky; (b) the near torii post box (1823,410,152x293) detail must rise from 1.43 to >= 4.5, approaching the 6.2-6.9 the same material reaches in the torii and hero shots; (c) distant mountains must keep their aerial perspective — phone-wide-r15 box (1013,117,380x117) must stay within saturation 0.16-0.24 and luma p50 within +/-15 of its current 160.5, so the fix is a near/mid-field ramp change and not a global fog reduction. Capture metadata reports fogDensity 0.0088 for reference.
